name: British Sea Power
label: Rough Trade
lede: Rough Trade signed a Brighton band who decorated stages with branches, gave journalists grid references and played a slate mine, a ferry and the highest pub in Britain. Twenty years later they won a Bafta for a video game and dropped the "British."

hero.by: British Sea Power in 2009. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: British Air Powers, at the end of the pier
eras.text: Two brothers and a school friend from outside Kendal in Cumbria met a guitarist from Bury in Reading, then moved the band to Brighton. There they ran their own club night, put out a single on their own label and caught the eye of the man who had just signed the Strokes.

years.h: A noticeboard ad at Reading University starts British Air Powers
years.p: Jan Scott Wilkinson, known as Yan, and guitarist [[Martin Noble|6d0d99b6-6d79-43da-9777-388c1b6a513d]] recruit fellow student Alison Cotton. Yan's brother Neil Hamilton Wilkinson and their school friend [[Matthew Wood|7311c105-e3da-4b40-9c72-4300f9ba2f99]] come down from Cumbria soon after.
years.xp:
The Wilkinson brothers grew up in a council house in rural Cumbria with parents from a much older generation; their father, Ronald, had fought in the Second World War. "Although the Lake District is a beautiful place to grow up in, it's pretty boring," Yan told the Guardian.

Cotton was later headhunted by the Reading band Saloon and left before the band made a record. One of the songs on the British Air Powers demo was called British Sea Power. It became Carrion.

years.h: Club Sea Power: folk singers, a 1940s fashion show and the band
years.p: In Brighton they host their own nights at the Freebutt and the Lift. Support comes from the Copper Family, a Sussex folk dynasty going back 200 years.

years.h: Fear of Drowning comes out on their own Golden Chariot label
years.p: A small run. The B-side, A Wooden Horse, borrows its sleeve from the dust jacket of a 1950 book about an Allied escape from a German POW camp.

years.h: [[Geoff Travis|70437714-3183-4916-947f-e5ba2154d16a]] sees them live and signs them to Rough Trade
years.p: It was the same year the relaunched label took on [[The Strokes|f181961b-20f7-459e-89de-920ef03c7ed0]], with [[The Libertines|82b304c0-7da4-45d3-896a-0767c7ae1141]] close behind. Travis reportedly told the band they could sell zero copies of their first album and still make a second.

years.cap: Eamon Hamilton in Official Fleet Reserve gear
years.h: [[Eamon Hamilton|1f729bfc-a193-42a5-aaf7-9ff8997cadcd]] joins on keyboards and a marching bass drum
years.p: The four-piece becomes five.

eras.title: Foliage, plastic birds and Rock in A
eras.text: The debut made critics fans and the shows made the band a word-of-mouth event: branches on the stage, stuffed birds on the amps, and a closing jam that could run past twenty minutes. The odder the venue, the better.

yt: Remember Me and Carrion on Later... with Jools Holland, October 2003
years.h: The Decline of British Sea Power, on Rough Trade
years.p: Critics loved it, and Carrion, the old song that once carried the band's name, becomes their first top 40 single.
play: The Decline of British Sea Power

years.cap: A stage invasion at a British Sea Power show
years.h: Time Out's live band of the year climb the rigging and tear down the trees
years.p: Stages come dressed in branches and plastic birds. The closer, Rock in A, can run past 20 minutes while Eamon Hamilton wanders the crowd with his drum and an eight-foot bear named Ursine Ultra joins the encore.
years.xp:
The foliage had its risks. Neil Wilkinson once climbed a tree to collect branches and sawed off the one he was sitting on, the band told the Observer.

The Time Out award came with a party in a Russian town Noble remembered as Mosquito, for what he called Russian gangsters, the magazine and a bed shop. "There were beds everywhere. Nobody cared about us," he said. A swimming pool sat where the audience should have been.

years.cap: British Sea Power on a stage dressed with foliage
years.h: Grid references instead of meeting places
years.p: Journalists got Ordnance Survey coordinates and a time. Tours took in the Scillonian Club on the Isles of Scilly, Grasmere Village Hall, the Czech Embassy in London and Carnglaze Caverns in Cornwall.
years.xp: The Observer's Tim Jonze was once sent off with a grid reference and ended up lost in the Sussex countryside. Over the years the band also played a Cornish slate mine, the Great Wall of China and the Natural History Museum, among the dinosaur skeletons.

years.h: Open Season cleans up the sound and reaches number 13
years.p: It Ended on an Oily Stage goes to number 18 the week before. The band also turn up on the BBC's Countryfile, playing Canvey Island outdoors.
play: It Ended on an Oily Stage

years.cap: British Sea Power under their banner
years.h: Eamon Hamilton leaves for Brakes; [[Phil Sumner|d1d5dc47-9b0c-4baa-8c81-ac2fd92ace1a]] arrives
years.p: Hamilton goes full-time with his own band. Sumner takes over keyboards and adds cornet.

eras.title: Do you like rock music?
eras.text: The third album went top 10, got a Mercury nomination and took the band to Letterman. The gigs got stranger to match: a hotel on Canvey Island, a pub at the top of the Pennines.

years.h: Do You Like Rock Music? puts them in the UK top 10
years.p: Produced with Graham Sutton. Waving Flags, a song welcoming new arrivals to Britain, becomes the band's calling card, and in July the album is nominated for the Mercury Prize.

years.h: Sumner's swan dive at the Leeds Irish Centre
years.p: He jumped from a 12-foot PA stack, was knocked out and went to hospital, then played the next night anyway.
years.xp: Sumner's own count, to the Observer: "Twelve stitches, three smashed teeth." When Wood hurt his back before the tour, Thomas White of Electric Soft Parade and Brakes filled in on drums.

years.h: Cumbrian wrestlers and a Bulgarian choir on Later
years.p: Jools Holland's show gets Waving Flags, Canvey Island and No Lucifer. Then a gig at the Monico Hotel on Canvey Island itself, with Wilko Johnson of Dr. Feelgood in the encore.

years.h: [[Abi Fry|78201620-0fd1-4076-b7df-fd7553c1b259]] tours on viola, then stays
years.p: She becomes a permanent member as the band play Glastonbury, Reading and Leeds, T in the Park and Bestival.

years.h: Sing Ye From the Hillsides! at the highest pub in Britain
years.p: The band's own festival at the Tan Hill Inn in the Yorkshire Dales. They did it again in 2010.

years.h: A new score for Man of Aran
years.p: Their soundtrack to Robert Flaherty's 1934 film about Irish fishermen, premiered live at the British Film Institute in April.

eras.title: Valhalla, Jodrell Bank and a monthly club
eras.text: A fourth rock album made in a freezing Sussex farmhouse, a gig under a radio telescope, and six months of writing a new EP every month for their Brighton club.

years.h: Top of the bill on the Festival Republic Stage at Reading and Leeds
years.p: That autumn they open for the [[Manic Street Preachers|32efea44-6cb5-4b4f-bdaa-c8b8f6cef981]] across Britain and put out the Zeus maxi EP.

q: The worst financial decision was calling ourselves British Sea Power.
years.h: Valhalla Dancehall, from a farmhouse with mice and crazy golf
years.p: Yan explained the title to the Observer. Recorded partly on the Isle of Skye and partly at the East Sussex farmhouse where he lived for 18 months.
years.xp:
Yan turned the farmhouse garden into a nine-hole crazy-golf course and learned the hard way about heating oil. "The band would turn up and be unhappy because it was so cold you could see your breath."

The name joke had a serious edge. "When we named ourselves, Britain seemed to be moving on to a bright future," he said. "Now it's a bit embarrassing."

years.h: Under the radio telescope at Jodrell Bank, with [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]]
years.p: Earlier, in May, three small shows at Berwick Village Hall in East Sussex marked ten years since Fear of Drowning.

years.h: Do It for Your Mum: their manager's book, on Rough Trade Books
years.p: Roy Wilkinson, older brother of Yan and Neil, wrote about managing the band and how their octogenarian father became its most devoted fan.

years.h: Six monthly EPs become Machineries of Joy
years.p: Through the first half of 2012 they wrote and released a new EP each month for their Krankenhaus club nights in Brighton, then re-recorded the best of them.

eras.title: Brass bands, a Bafta, a new name
eras.text: The band went their own way: brass-band tours, a crowdfunded album, a festival in a Cumbrian castle and a video-game score that won a Bafta. In 2021 they dropped the word that had dogged them for twenty years.

years.h: Sea of Brass, and the debut played in full with Eamon Hamilton back
years.p: After touring with local brass bands in late 2014, they release the album. Then a 12th-anniversary run of The Decline of British Sea Power in Brighton, Manchester and London.

years.h: Fans pay for Let the Dancers Inherit the Party
years.p: The album was crowdfunded and released on March 31. That summer they play Glastonbury.

years.h: Krankenhaus Festival opens at Muncaster Castle
years.p: The band's own festival, in their home county of Cumbria. It returned in 2022 and in 2023 won BBC 6 Music listeners' festival of the year.

years.h: A Bafta for the Disco Elysium score
years.p: Their 2019 soundtrack to the role-playing game wins Best Music at the BAFTA Games Awards.

years.big: "The people who gave us the most grief basically explain why."
years.h: British Sea Power become Sea Power
years.p: The band cited a rise in an isolationist, antagonistic kind of nationalism they didn't want to be confused with. Yan's line to the Guardian is above.
years.xp:
Noble called the old name "a monkey on our backs." The only real complaints came from social media and the right-wing press, Yan said, plus some fans who'd made their own Sea Power T-shirts because the merch wasn't ready.

Ursine Ultra the bear retired with the old name.

years.h: Everything Was Forever reaches number 4
years.p: Back with Graham Sutton. Yan said Two Fingers was the kind of song their late father Ronald, the band's biggest fan, would have told them to make.

years.cap: Abi Fry with Sea Power at the Roundhouse, London
years.h: Matthew Wood retires; Thomas White takes the drums
years.p: Wood had played with the Wilkinson brothers since their school days near Kendal.

sources.title: The Observer: British Sea Power, well, they're superstars at B&Q (Tim Jonze, 2011)
The Guardian: Sea Power, 'The people who gave us the most grief are why we changed our name' (Luke Turner, 2021)
